main_text.p: urget, effervescentes humores semper calidos esse, imò eos incendi & confagrare, uti pag. 41. 44. &c. injurius est in Sylvium qui, (uti vel ex ipso scripto Doctoris Le Vasseur constat) diserte docet pro ratione humorum effervescentium excitari effervescentiam frigidiorem, calidiorem & blandam, quod ut falsissimum, Sylvio sæpè exprobravit, supra non semel demonstrare coacti fuimus. si verò sententia Doctoris Le Vasseur, ex Sylvii hypothesi erronea sit obortâ nempè effervescentiâ calidâ venam cavam descendentem pulsare quod objicit Le Vasseur, certè magis magisque suam prodit famam, utpotè qui auctoritate cujusdam seductus palàm ostendit sibi prorsus ignotum esse quid sit Pulsus & quâ vi fiat. Etenim pag. 31. ex Galeno negat arterias, vi caloris & spiritûs à corde in eas influentis, dilatari: sed quâdam facultate quam arteriarum cordi continuarum tunicæ semper

page.notes: The running head reads "FL. SCHUYL" with the spaced small capitals as printed. The scan has a few marks in the margins, which are not text. The word "confagrare" appears as printed; the reading "confl agrare" is likely "conflagrare" with a ligature, but it is transcribed as the printed form. The phrase "magisque" in "magis ma-gisque" is a line-end hyphenation; it is given as printed "magisque suam prodit" with the hyphen joined.
